Abstract.AbstractText: Glioblastoma is a lethal disease featured with a high proliferation of tumor cells, excessive angiogenesis, and heavydrug resistance. The overall survival of glioblastoma patients was dismal even with intensive standard care. Recent advantages in immune checkpoint blockades are changing the treatment of cancers. However, the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockades in glioblastoma were unclear. Here, we investigated the roles of CD103<sup>+</sup> cells in regulating the effects of immune checkpoint blockades in glioblastoma mouse models. Our findings indicated that in the murine glioblastoma model was not sensitive to immune checkpoint blockades. Flt3L, a growth factor of CD103<sup>+</sup> cells, could significantly increase the number of CD103<sup>+</sup> dendritic cells in murine glioblastoma model, and thus sensitize murine glioblastoma to immune checkpoint blockades. Downstream analyses indicated that the Flt3L and immune checkpoint blockades combination increased number of tumor-infiltrating CD8<sup>+</sup> cells, decreased immune checkpoint expression, therefore enhanced anti-tumor immune response in murine glioblastoma model. These findings suggested that Flt3L could enhance the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockades in glioblastoma via expanding CD103<sup>+</sup> dendritic cells and downstream anti-tumor immune response.
